output.reason: A 68-year-old with COPD reporting two days of worsening dyspnea now breathless walking to the bathroom with green phlegm needs hands-on assessment today — oxygen saturation, lung exam and chest imaging — which messaging cannot provide.
output.patientMessage: Please be seen in person today — an urgent care or emergency department can check your oxygen level, listen to your chest and get a chest X-ray. Breathlessness just walking to the bathroom with COPD and green phlegm needs same-day assessment. Call 911 right away if you struggle to speak in full sentences, your lips or fingers look blue, you feel faint, or you become confused. Don't wait for a message reply.
differential: Pneumonia or other complication (e.g. PE, heart failure) causing the dyspnea

redFlags.quote: now I'm winded just walking to the bathroom

output.vitalSigns: No oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, heart rate or temperature reported; whether any were measured is unknown.
output.evidenceLimitations: No measured oxygenation or exam findings are available, and the cited sources are ED reference syntheses, not telehealth protocols.

citations.claim: Sustained worsening of dyspnea with increased sputum purulence beyond usual variation defines an exacerbation requiring a change in therapy.
citations.limitation: Severity cannot be graded remotely without vitals or exam.

citations.claim: Dyspnea in COPD may reflect pneumothorax, PE or heart failure, so chest imaging is advised rather than assuming COPD alone.
citations.limitation: Written for ED-based evaluation, not initial remote triage.
